name: ISREF
description: ISREF returns TRUE if the supplied value is a cell or range reference (or a function that returns one), and FALSE otherwise.
tldr: Tests whether a value is a reference.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value, cell reference, or formula result to test.

basicExample.explanation: A1 is a cell reference, so ISREF returns TRUE.

advancedExamples.title: A text address is not a reference
advancedExamples.description: Show that text naming a cell is not a reference
advancedExamples.explanation: "A1" is text, not an actual reference, so ISREF returns FALSE.

advancedExamples.title: Reference-returning functions
advancedExamples.scenario: Convert a text address into a real reference.
advancedExamples.description: INDIRECT returns a reference, so ISREF is TRUE
advancedExamples.explanation: INDIRECT evaluates to a reference, which ISREF detects.

howItWorks: ISREF returns TRUE if the value is a cell or range reference, or the result of a function that returns a reference such as INDIRECT or OFFSET. Plain values, text, and most value-returning functions return FALSE.

howToSteps.name: Pick the value
howToSteps.text: Select the value or formula to test.

howToSteps.name: Read the result
howToSteps.text: TRUE means it is a reference.

limitations: A text string like "A1" is not a reference even though it names one.
Most functions return values, not references, so ISREF returns FALSE for them.
Rarely needed outside advanced formula validation.

commonErrors.fix: Use INDIRECT to turn a text address into a real reference.

commonErrors.cause: A function like OFFSET returns a reference.
commonErrors.fix: Expected behavior; ISREF detects reference-returning functions.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISREF works identically in Google Sheets with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: Does INDIRECT make ISREF TRUE?
faq.answer: Yes, because INDIRECT returns a reference.

faq.question: Is a named range a reference?
faq.answer: Yes, ISREF returns TRUE for a valid named range.

faq.question: When would I use ISREF?
faq.answer: Mostly in advanced formulas that validate whether an argument is a reference, or with CHOOSE/INDIRECT tricks.
